source_locator.description: Gunasekaran deliberately babbles as though mad.

translation.english_text: [He is deliberately babbling as though mad.]

notes: The source's mock-royal register and onomatopoeic `டுமீர்` are retained rather than normalized into realistic court dialogue.
translation.english_text: Did he teach us to boil stones and earth... and drink them? (He laughs.) I am the Maharaja myself—no doubt about it! Who are they? Ministers and chief ministers, come! Sit on this seat! Let the Bharatanatyam begin—dumeer, dumeer, dumeer!

notes: The source block is unlabelled and is not a verified soundtrack occurrence. Scene context places it inside Gunasekaran's performed babbling, so it is source-located as dialogue-like performance without inventing a song occurrence ID.
The line breaks preserve the source's play among `வேணு / கோபாலன் / நந்தகோபாலன்`; the English does not collapse the name/sound sequence.
english_lines: I will dance with Gopalan—with Nanda
I will dance like a cuckoo of music.

source_locator.description: Unlabelled mock-royal, political and devotional performance by Gunasekaran.

notes: This source block is unlabelled but occurs inside Gunasekaran's deliberate madman performance; it is source-located without inventing a dialogue-record ID.
`மாதம் மும்மாரி மழை` retains the idealized `three times a month` rain formula rather than being modernized.
The verified source forms `கடக்கட்டு` and `வாட் வசிக்குதா?` are semantically opaque. They are exposed as `kadakkattu` and `What—vasikkudha?` rather than silently assigned invented meanings.
`பவுன் விளையுற நாடு` is rendered as a land where gold sovereigns grow; `பரதேசி` is retained as `paradesi` in the source's insulting/social register.
The code-switched English-like forms (`வேர் யு ஆர்`, `வாட் யு வாண்ட்`) remain deliberately nonstandard in English, reflecting the source performance.
The closing devotional chant is transliterated conservatively from the verified Tamil rather than standardized from an external liturgical source.
translation.english_text: Ayyo! Ayyo! Enough, enough! Let the inquiry into the realm begin—dum, dum, dum! Minister, does rain fall three times a month in our great city? Dumeer! Dumeer! That's why we've tied a 'kadakkattu' for Lord Varuna and sent a telegram, Maharaja! Bravo, bravo! Who are they? Why are they shouting? Oi, oi, Maharaja, we cannot bear the hunger in our bellies—we are dying, family after family. What—vasikkudha? Don't say that, sinner! This is a land where gold sovereigns grow! You paradesi fellows, are you starving? Die—die happily! Only then will the comet rise. Sir—sir—r, Maharaja, no money? Where you are! What else you want? Carry kavadi for Vadamalaiyan—For Vadamalaiyan... (He picks up a brick.) Arohara! Sarvarama Sanjeevi Nama Parvatham, Rama Sankeerthanam... Govinda... Hare Govinda!

source_locator.description: Gunasekaran places the brick on the roadside load-rest.

translation.english_text: (He places the brick on the roadside load-rest.)

source_locator.description: Unlabelled planted-stone verse performed by Gunasekaran.

notes: The source does not attribute this verse and the verified song inventory does not classify it as a soundtrack or quoted-verse occurrence. It therefore remains a scene-located unlabelled performance unit; no external authorship is introduced.
`நட்டகல்` is retained literally as a `planted stone`; the rhetorical attack on ritual is not softened.
english_lines: You call a planted stone a god and deck it with four flowers;
You circle it, muttering and muttering—what mantra is that?
Will the planted stone speak when the Lord is within?
Can a fired pot and ladle know the taste of the curry?

english_lines: Let us sing bhajans, Kannan's name, while starving;
Let us sing bhajans, Kannan's name.
Let us sing bhajans, Kannan's name—while starving;
Let us sing bhajans, Kannan's name.

source_locator.description: Kalyani sees Gunasekaran speaking in many guises like a madman.

translation.english_text: (Kalyani sees Gunasekaran, who in this way speaks in many guises like a madman.)
Ayyo—poor thing—someone seems to be mad.
Little sister, little sister, come here.
What? So I'm your little sister?
Yes! For two or three days I've been thinking of telling you something.

notes: The source has the male Gunasekaran absurdly promise `நான் ஒரு பொண்ணு பெத்து தர்றேன்`; the English preserves the madman proposal rather than rationalizing it as finding someone else's daughter.
translation.english_text: Nothing... I'll have a daughter—will you arrange for her to marry your son?

notes: `சீதனம்` is rendered as `dowry` here because Kalyani explicitly answers the proposed marriage arrangement; this differs from its broader ceremonial-gift sense in the scene-17 lullaby.

translation.english_text: We can see about that later. First, let me hold my 'son-in-law' for a moment—I'll give him a kiss and hand him back.

notes: The closing source form `தாளா துயரத்தோடு` is compressed; `with unbearable sorrow` is a contextual English rendering, not a Tamil correction.
translation.english_text: Little sister, just once! Won't you let me hold him? Little sister, I swear—I'm not mad. I won't harm your child. Won't you let me hold him? Yes, I am mad. (He goes away with unbearable sorrow.)
